acceptance: Every open item is searched for criteria requiring deliberate CPU, memory or disk load; the list of matches is recorded.
Each match is rewritten to cite a test that injects the reading, or the item records why real load is unavoidable and that it must run under make heavy-run.
No agent instruction or skill text is changed.
context: Found during a retrospective on 2026-11-15. Tracker-only work; the planning session is the tracker writer. Guardrails: linked worktree, one PR; no live-cloud runs; heavy work only via lock-taking entry points; re-verify cited facts before acting.
description:
Problem: the acceptance criterion for bundle-record-host-load-20261113 asked for a smoke run 'beside a deliberate CPU load'. To meet it an agent started 2 x CPU-count spin loops on a shared host; they leaked and ran about 20 hours, tainting other measurements. A criterion that can only be met by loading a shared host is the defect; the behaviour it checks is covered by unit tests that fake the sampler.

Outcome: no open tracker item carries a criterion that requires real host load, and each replaced criterion names the faked-sampler or injected-reading test that stands in for it.
